stories.title: Progressives grow sway in Lansing, push to tax the rich and corporations
stories.summary: Incoming House Speaker Ranjeev Puri of Canton will navigate a Michigan Legislature with a growing progressive caucus in 2027. This group aims to push for policies like increased corporate income tax, government ethics reforms, and potentially a state-level single-payer healthcare system, though the latter faces leadership resistance. Puri will need to balance these ambitions with the broader caucus's agenda.

stories.title: U-M addiction specialist warns of kratom health risks
stories.summary: A University of Michigan addiction specialist warns that kratom products, particularly those containing synthetic opioids like 7-OH, can affect the brain similarly to fentanyl and heroin, leading to addiction. Plymouth Township has enacted its own restrictions on kratom sales, while statewide legislation remains stalled.

inputFacts.title: U-M addiction specialist warns of kratom health risks
inputFacts.summary: As Michigan House Bill 5537 remains stalled in the state Senate, some local communities are enacting their own bans on kratom sales. University of Michigan addiction specialist Eliza Hutchinson warns that synthetic opioids found in these products can lead to rapid addiction and pose significant health risks.

editorial.reason: The article discusses health risks associated with kratom, a substance that has prompted local civic action in Plymouth Township, a community directly adjacent to Canton. The stalled state legislation and local responses make this a relevant local issue.

stories.title: Ypsi Township to hold panel discussion at EMU on U-M/Los Alamos project
stories.summary: Ypsilanti Township will host a panel discussion at Eastern Michigan University regarding the proposed University of Michigan/Los Alamos National Laboratory computing research center. The discussion will include the executive director of Nuclear Watch New Mexico, who has expressed concerns about the partnership's implications for AI and nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Zoning can make or break small business success
stories.summary: Dexter's evolving zoning ordinances, including changes for mixed-use development and outdoor dining, have supported its local economy and small businesses. Experts suggest that municipalities should review zoning to reduce barriers for entrepreneurs, as complex regulations can hinder business establishment and growth, impacting local vitality.

stories.title: Faculty Senate passes vote of no confidence in UMPD and University’s handling of GEO negotiations
stories.summary: The University of Michigan Faculty Senate passed a vote of no confidence in the University's handling of Graduate Employees' Organization (GEO) negotiations and the University of Michigan Police Department (UMPD). This vote was part of a broader motion expressing solidarity with GEO and pro-Palestine activists, and criticizing the administration's response to activism.

The vote reflects growing faculty dissatisfaction with institutional leadership and campus safety policies.

stories.title: World premiere of oratorio 'Don't Let the Sun' at U-M
stories.summary: The University of Michigan will premiere "Don't Let the Sun," an oratorio exploring the history of "sundown towns" in the U.S., including their prevalence outside the South. The work, commissioned by U-M, aims to educate audiences on this hidden dimension of American history and encourage reflection on building welcoming communities.

inputFacts.title: World premiere of oratorio 'Don't Let the Sun' at U-M
inputFacts.summary: A new oratorio titled 'Don't Let the Sun' explores the history of sundown towns in America. Inspired by sociologist James Loewen, the work will be performed by the U-M Chamber Choir and University Choir at Hill Auditorium on November 17.

inputFacts.title: Federal judge considers rare review of grand jury proceedings in U-M protest case
inputFacts.summary: A federal judge is considering an unusual request to review grand jury testimony in the case of Zainab Hakim, one of 12 individuals charged in connection with pro-Palestinian protests. The defense argues that prosecutors may have presented misleading information regarding an alleged evidence-tampering incident involving a laptop during an FBI raid. The judge has adjourned the bail hearing until December 2 to research legal precedents for unsealing grand jury proceedings.

inputFacts.title: Ann Arbor drivers are failing to use turn signals, placing cyclists under threat
inputFacts.summary: Despite receiving a gold-level Bicycle Friendly Community award in 2022, Ann Arbor continues to see a high average of vehicle-bicycle accidents. The report highlights ongoing safety concerns for cyclists due to driver negligence, specifically the failure to use turn signals.

inputFacts.title: ‘There has to be accountability’: University of Michigan ‘monitoring situation’ after Andrew Marsh charge
inputFacts.summary: University of Michigan wide receiver Andrew Marsh is facing a misdemeanor indecent exposure charge following an incident involving a food delivery driver in Pittsfield Township on February 2. The university stated it is monitoring the situation, and Marsh is scheduled for arraignment on December 2.

inputFacts.title: Narratives Beyond the Battlefield: EMU Event Explores How Stories Shape Our Understanding of War
inputFacts.summary: Eastern Michigan University is hosting a public event titled 'Narrative of War in Life, Literature, and Film'. The discussion will explore how various storytelling mediums influence our perception of conflict.

inputFacts.title: Detroit’s Holiday Tradition Shines with 23rd Annual Detroit Tree Lighting
inputFacts.summary: The 23rd annual Detroit Tree Lighting at Campus Martius Park features a variety of musical performances, local food vendors, and holiday activities. The event also supports the community through the Mittens for Detroit donation drive and kicks off the winter season with the opening of The Rink at Campus Martius Park.

inputFacts.title: Detroit ‘Sleep Out’ raises awareness, funds to fight youth homelessness
inputFacts.summary: Covenant House hosted its 13th annual Detroit Sleep Out to raise awareness and funds for youth homelessness, which has seen a 27% increase since 2021. Participants spent the night in cardboard boxes and tarps to stand in solidarity with young people experiencing housing instability.

inputFacts.title: Mild for tree lighting, tipoff, touchdowns: Metro Detroit’s weather delivers before major reversal
inputFacts.summary: Metro Detroit is experiencing near-record warmth with temperatures reaching 65 degrees, significantly above the seasonal average. These mild conditions are expected to persist through the weekend for local events before a sharp cooldown and rain arrive early next week.
